 JUDGMENT
The petitioner has filed claim application U/Sec 166 of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1989, seeking compensation on account of the grievous injuries sustained by him in the Motor Vehicle Accident.

02. The brief facts of the petitioner case as follows:-
On 11.12.2022 at about 01.30 p.m, the petitioner was travelling in his two-wheeler Scooter bearing No.KA-04-KD-5498 from his home MEI Junction to (SCCH-3) 3 M.V.C.No.2196/2023 Peenya for office duty, when he reached opposite to Hyundai Car Showroom, Goraguntepalya, Tumkur Road, at the same time, the Car of the respondent No.1 bearing No.KA-04-MA-6429 and the same was driven by respondent No.2, rashly and negligently with a high speed and dashed against the petitioner's two-wheeler and caused the accident.
Due to which, the petitioner sustained grievous injuries.

Immediately after the accident, the petitioner was shifted to the footpath when the respondent No.2 got down from the car and introduce himself as a doctor having Shyamal Clinic at Mathikere and enquired to the petitioner and shifted to his car for giving treatment at his clinic, the respondent No.2 has given first aid and treatment to the petitioner and further assured that if more treatment required to the petitioner and sent the petitioner home by Auto rickshaw.

On 12.12.2022 the right leg of the petitioner was swelling and pain has not reduced and, the petitioner went for further treatment at K.C. General hospital and taken the X-ray, the injuries in the body swelling and deformity of right foot and abrasions over right knee and abrasions and tenderness plus on right shoulder, therefore the doctor informed that the right (SCCH-3) 4 M.V.C.No.2196/2023 leg foot bone were cracked and it is required more treatment and bedrest for more than 6 months and the doctor had given treatment by covering cement plaster and advised to the petitioner to take 6 months bedrest and he has taken continues treatment for about more than 4 months and incurred Rs.2,00,000/- towards treatment, hospital charges and losses of income and other etc., and discharged with an advise of doctor for follow-up treatment and 6 months bedrest.
The petitioner has try to contact the respondents No.1 and 2 through by phone for further more treatment, but both did not respond to the petitioner call, however the petitioner has lodged complaint against respondent No.2 at Yeshwanthpura Traffic Police Station as driver of offending car.

Prior to the accident, the petitioner was hale Mahadevaswamy.P vs Dr. Sunitha B. Todakar on 3 December, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/34305013/
2 and healthy and was aged about 43 years and was working as a Painter at TTP Technology Pvt. Ltd., and earning Rs.36,000/- p.m. Due to accidental injuries, he is not able to do his work by going independently and he has been depending on others and has suffered mentally, physically and financially.

sentences.text: The accident occurred due to rash and negligent driving by the driver of offending car by respondent No.2.

Hence,
the respondent No.1 (SCCH-3) 5 M.V.C.No.2196/2023 being the owner and the respondent No.2 being the driver of the said offending car, are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation of Rs.10,00,000/- with cost and interest at the rate of 12%
p.a.
03.
On service of notice, the respondents No.1 and 2 have appeared before the tribunal through their counsels and have filed objections.

04. The respondents in their objections has denied the entire case of the petitioner and further denied the alleged accident, negligence of the driver of offending car, age, income, occupation of the petitioner and nature of the injuries sustained by the petitioner and treatment taken by the petitioner and expenses incurred by the petitioner and contended that the alleged accident caused due to negligence on the part of the petitioner and there is no fault, rash and negligent driving on the part of the driver of the car.
The petition is bad for non-joinder of necessary parties and the compensation claimed is highly exaggerated and pray for dismiss the petition with costs against the respondents.

05. Based on the aforesaid pleadings, the following issues have been framed by my learned predecessor: -
 (SCCH-3) 6 M.V.C.No.2196/2023  ISSUES 01.

Whether the petitioner proves that he has sustained grievous injuries in the accident occurred on 11.12.2022 at about 01.30 p.m, opposite Hyundai Car Showroom, Goraguntepalya Junction, Tumkur Road, Bengaluru, due to rash and negligent driving of Car bearing registration No.KA-04-MA-6429 by its driver as alleged in the petition?
02. Whether the petitioner is entitled for compensation?
If so, to what amount and from whom?
06 . What Order or Award?
06. In order to prove the case, the petitioner got examined himself as PW.1 and got marked 23 documents as Ex.P.1 to 23 and closed his side evidence.
07. By way of rebuttal, the respondent No.2 got examined himself as RW.1 and got marked 4 documents as Ex.R.1 to 4 and closed his side evidence.

09. My findings on the aforesaid issues are as under:-
 Issue No.1
In affirmative  Issue No.2 In partly affirmative  Issue No.3

As per final order  for the following:
 (SCCH-3) 7 M.V.C.No.2196/2023  REASONS 10.
Issue No.1:- The petitioner in order to prove his case, he himself examined as PW.1 and in his chief-examination evidence he has reiterated the petition averments therein.
Though he has been elaborately cross-examined by the respondents counsel, but nothing is brought on record to disbelieve the case of the petitioner.

On perusal of exhibited documents, Ex.P.3 is the Wound certificate shows petitioner sustained swelling, deformity of right foot, abrasion over right knee,
abrasion and tenderness on right shoulder and doctor opined that said injuries are simple in nature.
Ex.P.4 is the FIR registered at Yeshwanthapura Traffic Police against driver/respondent No.2 of the Car.
Ex.P.5 is the complaint which shows that, due to the rash and negligent driving by the driver of the car the accident took place and petitioner sustained grievous injuries.

Ex.P.6 is the Charge sheet filed against driver/respondent No.2 and owner of the offending car as A1 and A2 for the offences punishable U/Sec 279, 337 of IPC and Sections 134(B), 187, 3(1), 181, 56, 192, 146, 196, 5 and 180 of IMV Act for rash and negligent driving and the owner has entrusted the car (SCCH-3) 8 M.V.C.No.2196/2023 to the person who did not possessed driving licence and there is no fitness certificate to the car at the time of accident and after causing the accident the driver has not informed about the accident to the Police.

Ex.P.7 and 8 are the Spot Mahazar and Sketch showing place of accident opposite to Hyundai Car Showroom, between Goraguntepalya and CMTI Junction,
Tumkur Road, wherein the offending car came from East to West on right side of the road and dashed against the scooter which was going on the left side of the road, which is not disputed.
Ex.P.10 and P.10(a) are Photographs and CD of petitioner, Ex.P.18 is Notice U/Sec.133 of IMV Act issued to the owner of the offending Car.

Ex.P.19 is copy of Reply to notice which discloses that the owner of the offending Car has stated that respondent No.2 was driving the car at the time of accident and he had no driving licence and no insurance and fitness certificate to the offending car as on the date of accident.
Ex.P.20 is IMV report which shows involvement of offending car in the accident.
Ex.P.21 is IMV report which shows involvement of petitioner's two-wheeler in the accident.
Ex.P.22 is Seizer Mahazar shows after investigation the Police (SCCH-3) 9 M.V.C.No.2196/2023 have seized both the vehicles and Ex.P.23 is Photographs of offending car and two-wheeler.

To disprove the petitioner case, the respondent No.2 got examined himself as RW.1 and in his chief- examination evidence he has deposed that he was driving offending car as on the date of accident and it was raining and there was heavy traffic on the road and they heard a noise and they stopped Mahadevaswamy.

sentences.text: the car and got down, the petitioner was riding two-wheeler had fallen down behind their car and sustained simple injury and their car not touched to the petitioner's two- wheeler and he tried to lodge a complaint before the Yeshawanthpura Traffic Police but they refused to receive his complaint and thereafter they sent complaint through registered post and he has produced Complaint sent by post, Complaint sent to Police Commissioner, Postal receipts and Endorsement given by Yashwanthpura Police Station as per Ex.R1 to 4 and also got marked Ex.P.18 to 20 in his cross-examination.

In his cross-examination he admits that respondent No.1 is his wife, she also doctor and he was running Health Clinic and his wife running Shyamala Clinic and denied to the suggestion that the said car did not have insurance on 11.12.2022.
That (SCCH-3) 10 M.V.C.No.2196/2023 insurance certificate can be given to the court.
I had a driving license at the time of the accident.
The driving license can be presented to the court.
It is true that heavy vehicles ply on the MES route.
It is true that I did not have a driving license to drive the car on the day of the accident and I did not have experience in driving a car.
It is true that a case is pending against him and his wife before JMFC Court.
The evidence and cross-examination of RW.1 reveals that at the time of accident the respondent No.2 was driven the car and it was no insurance and he had no valid driving licence.
Hence, the evidence of RW.1 is not helpful to the case of the respondents.

The oral and documentary evidence produced by the petitioner clearly goes to show that, due to the rash and negligent driving by the driver of the offending Car the accident took place and petitioner sustained grievous injuries.
Accordingly, Issue No.1 is answered in the affirmative.
11. Issue No.2:- This issue is related to the entitlement of the compensation on account of grievous injuries sustained by the petitioner in Road traffic accident.

The petitioner in his evidence and pleadings has stated that prior to accident he was hale and healthy and was aged about 43 years and was working as a Painter at TTP Technology Pvt. Ltd., and earning Rs.36,000/- p.m and has spent Rs.2,00,000/- towards treatment, hospital charges.

On account of accidental injuries, the petitioner is not able to do his work by going independently and he has been depending on others and has suffered mentally,
physically and financially.

12. It is duty of the petitioner to prove his age, but the petitioner has not produced birth certificate,
school records or SSLC marks card or Aadhaar card to show his exact date of birth.
However, he has produced Ex.P.11 Identity card issued by TTP Technologies Pvt. Ltd., which shows the date of birth of the petitioner is mentioned as 10.07.1979.
The alleged accident occurred on 11.12.2022.
Therefore, it appears that at the time of accident the age of petitioner is 43 years.
Accordingly, this tribunal has assessed the age of the petitioner as 43 years as on the date of accident.

13. As per Ex.P.3 Wound certificate the petitioner has sustained only simple injuries and he has not produced any Discharge summary to show (SCCH-3) 12 M.V.C.No.2196/2023 that he took treatment as inpatient.

But in this case the petitioner has not examined the doctor who treated him and has not produced any disability certificate to show that he has sustained any physical or functional disability which is come in the way of his day to day life.

As per Ex.P.16 the petitioner has Mahadevaswamy.P vs Dr. Sunitha B. Todakar on 3 December, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/34305013/
5 incurred Medical expenses of Rs.1,300/-.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
Absolutely there is no evidence on record to show that petitioner sustained any physical or functional disability and no evidence on record to show his age,
avocation and income.

There is no evidence on record to show that petitioner sustained loss of future income and loss of income during laid up period and also there is no evidence on record to show that petitioner requires further treatment.
Therefore, under the facts and circumstances of the case, this tribunal is of the opinion that the petitioner is entitled for total compensation of Rs.40,000/-.
14. Accordingly I hold that, the petitioner is entitled for total compensation of Rs.40,000/- with interest at the rate of 6% p.a from the date of petition till its realization.

15. Regarding liability:- On service of notice, respondents No.1 and 2 have appeared and filed (SCCH-3) 13 M.V.C.No.2196/2023 objections statement and contest the matter and respondent No.2 got examined as RW.1, but they have not proved their contention.
On the date of accident the offending vehicle had no policy and fitness certificate and driver had no driving licence.
Hence, respondents No.1 and 2 are jointly and severally liable to pay above said compensation amount.
Respondent No.1, owner of the offending vehicle is directed to deposit above said compensation amount within two months from the date of filing of the petition till the date of deposit.

Accordingly,
I answered Issue No.2 partly in affirmative.
16. Issue No.3:

In view of reasons assigned to Issue No.1 and 2, I proceed to pass the following:-
ORDER
The petition filed by the petitioner U/Sec.166 of the M.V. Act, 1989 is partly allowed with cost.
The petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs.40,000/- (Rupees Forty thousand only) with interest at the rate of 6% p.a from the date of petition till its realization.
The respondent No.1, owner of the offending vehicle shall deposit above said compensation amount (SCCH-3) 14 M.V.C.No.2196/2023 with interest within two months from the date of this Judgment.

On deposit of the compensation amount with interest, since the award amount is meager one, entire award amount is ordered to be released in favour of petitioner through E-payment directly to his account by obtaining his bank account details.
The Advocate fee is fixed at Rs.1,000/-.
Draw award accordingly.
